data.name: A Quiver of Crows
data.detailed_description:
A difficult twin-stick shmup set in a grim world cursed by demons and ghouls.

Frantic Battles in a Grim World

  • Unlike most shmups, this world is made up of flesh, bones, and dirt instead of the common rigid objects such as ships set in space.
  • Each enemy type has a unique set of behaviors.
  • Most foes do not follow preset patterns. Instead, they try to hunt you down.
  • Some enemies fly in close for melee combat. Others will shoot from a far away range.

Co-op Twin-Stick Action

  • The game blends the insanity of shmups with the free range of motion of twin-stick shooters.
  • Find a friend. Find a couch. Have tons of fun with the optional single-screen couch co-op!

Upgradeable Weapons, Bombs, and Shields

  • Collect and enhance a variety of weapons. Influenced by traditional shmups, watch as your weapons’ firing trajectory and pattern change with each upgrade.
  • From heat seeking quills to things that go BOOM, collect them all and use them to crush your foes!
  • Upgrade your shields to withstand relentless attacks.

Play on Windows, Mac, & Linux

  • Best played with a twin-stick controller. Steer with the left stick, aim with the right.
  • Never fear! You can also use your keyboard and mouse.

reviews.review:
[b] Target Audience: [/b] [I] Masochists [/i]

[b] Summary: [/b]  
A Quiver of Crows main problem has to do with its difficulty. And let's be real: Shoot em ups and top down shooters can be at their best when they've got the player being put into some of the most difficult situations. But there's a difference between Difficulty and Fairness: and the fairness elements is where A Quiver of Crows starts to fall apart. With high respawns and not giving you a reasonable set of tools to go after them with, a run can quickly fall into despair as you realize you just weren't going fast enough. You can speed off screen to get into the next section, then already have 10 enemies on top of you because of their relative speed against yours.

The main core problem here is the combination of the mechanics: each individual mechanic works such as the ragdoll corpses or the black aesthetic. But when they combine together, it becomes clear that one doesn't compliment the other: they sometimes fight each other. Sometimes the game wants you to go fast because of the respawn rate being so high. But at the same time, certain enemies need you to take time to go through, meaning you need to slow down. The dark aesthetic works well against light backgrounds: but when the same backgrounds is what you're firing against, and you lose those lasers into the backgrounds: you've got a problem.

I feel like the game itself needs major tweaking: but once that tweaking happens: there is something under the surface to enjoy here in the top-down/shoot em up genre. But until then, it's a game that will frustrate you in all the wrong ways. 

[b]Video Review: [/b] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2VuKfPr8MmI

[u] Lists: [/u]
[b]Positives:[/b]
[list]
[*] The simple style makes for a striking aesthetic, one that is really nice to look at. It's not Limbo persay, but the black does really do a good job of highlighting the action.
[*] The ragdoll corpses can be pretty hilarious at times.
[*] At the core, each of the different mechanics elements do work. Whether it be the speed the fights take place on or the strengths of the different weapons, they all have basic good design structures at the core.
[*] The upgrades giving more personality to weapons is nice to see. 
[*] Some of the enemy designs are rather interesting, and their variety in AI is good.
[*] The music is appropriate for the setting.
[*] No major performance issues.
[/list]

[b]Negatives:[/b]
[list]
[*] The Feel. What I mean by this is that the mechanics don't feel like that work together. For example, the game makes it clear that you need to avoid enemy damage, and taking your time on certain enemies is necessary. With that said, it then respawns enemies at a high rate....meaning you need to go fast. But you need to go slow as well. That's where the problem is: the game gives you conflicting messages.
[*] Laser and Fire effects can easily be lost in the background at times, which becomes a major problem in a game that has you dodging left and right.
[*] It can be really hard to tell if you're hitting something. Sure, you can tell if something is dead via the lack of red in the creature: but whether or not you're doing damage is a different story. And with the higher speed of gameplay here, you feel like you're just firing randomly at the air, hoping that something works. 
[*] Respawn rate versus Fire power doesn't seem to be of the right proportion. You can get overwhelmed easily in several stages. 
[*] While the corpses are hilarious, they get in the way especially in small corridors. This adds to the difficulty in a bad way. 
[*] Level design and enemy layout don't seem to work together well at times. Like the random locations that enemies spawn at don't make sense given the level design. 
[*] A lack of repeatability in Enemy AI that you can reasonably try to use. 
[*] The sound at times drills into your head and makes you want to blow out your ear drums. The fast forward attack (the green arrows) constant sound when firing is just so grating. 
[*] Weapons can be a little hard to understand their strengths versus each other. They are very subtle. 
[/list]

[b] If you want more reviews/information regarding games I've reviewed, visit my curator. [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/6861768/]Dragnix Curator [/url][/b]
